title: Pasta e Fagioli (Bean and Pasta Soup with Rosemary)
summary: A hearty Italian bean and pasta soup built on a sweet vegetable base and simmered with rosemary until thick and warming.
equipment: large heavy saucepan or casserole (at least 4 litres)

ingredients.item: 400 g tins cannellini or borlotti beans, drained and rinsed (about 480 g drained)
fine sea salt or table salt

steps.title: Build the Soffritto
steps.text: Warm the olive oil in the pan over medium heat and cook the onion, carrot and celery with a pinch of the salt for 8-10 minutes until soft and sweet but not browned. This slow start, known as a soffritto, builds a sweet vegetable base that underpins the whole soup.

steps.title: Add Garlic, Rosemary and Tomato Purée
steps.text: Stir in the garlic, rosemary and tomato purée, cooking for 1-2 minutes until the purée darkens slightly. Frying the purée briefly cooks off its raw, tinny edge and deepens its flavour before the liquid goes in.

steps.title: Simmer with Beans
steps.text: Add the beans, water, remaining salt and pepper, then bring to a simmer and cook for 15 minutes; lift out the rosemary sprig once it's done its job. This gentle simmer softens the beans further and lets their flavour spread through the broth.

steps.title: Blend Part of the Soup
steps.text: Blend or mash about a third of the soup in the pan, leaving the rest whole, so you get a creamy body without needing any cream. Breaking down some of the beans naturally thickens the broth while the whole beans and vegetables keep some texture.

steps.title: Cook the Pasta In the Soup
steps.text: Bring the soup back to a lively simmer, add the pasta and cook, stirring often so it doesn't stick to the base, for the packet time plus 1-2 minutes until tender, adding a splash of water if it gets too thick. Cooking the pasta directly in the soup lets it release starch into the broth, thickening it further as it sits.

steps.title: Taste and Serve
steps.text: Taste for salt before serving, then ladle into bowls and top with the grated Parmesan and a drizzle of olive oil. A finishing drizzle of good oil adds a fresh, fruity note that cooking alone can't give the soup.

tips: Don't rush the soffritto; letting the onion, carrot and celery soften slowly for the full 8-10 minutes builds a much sweeter base than cooking them hard and fast.
Stir the pasta often once it goes into the soup, as it's prone to sticking to the bottom of the pan.
Keep some beans whole when blending so the soup has both creaminess and texture.
The soup thickens a lot as it cools and sits, so loosen leftovers with a splash of water when reheating.
storage: Keep covered in the fridge for up to 3 days, or freeze for up to 3 months; the pasta softens further on freezing, so it's best added fresh if making ahead for the freezer. Reheat gently in a pan with a splash of water, stirring, until piping hot throughout. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
